learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the story of a pampered dog, the dangers of overfeeding, and how common sense can sometimes be the best medicine!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: शल्य चिकित्सा (यहाँ इसका अर्थ 'पशु चिकित्सालय' है)
बीमारी के बाद धीरे-धीरे ठीक होना

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Tricki is a small dog who is overly loved and overfed by his rich mistress, Mrs. Pumphrey. He becomes hugely fat, like a 'bloated sausage', and falls ill.
Thinking Tricki is suffering from malnutrition, she feeds him extra snacks like malt, cod-liver oil, and Horlicks, making his condition worse.
Mr. Herriot, a clever veterinary surgeon, takes Tricki to his hospital. He gives Tricki no medicine and no food for two days—only plenty of water and exercise with other dogs.
Tricki loses his excess fat, becomes energetic, and learns to fight for his food. He transforms into a flexible, hard-muscled animal.
When Mrs. Pumphrey sees a completely transformed and active Tricki, she cries out of joy and calls it a 'triumph of surgery', not knowing it was just diet control!

fun_activity.title: 🐕 Diet Plan for a Dog
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are Mr. Herriot. Write a strict 3-point 'Diet and Exercise Plan' for Tricki to give to Mrs. Pumphrey so he never gets fat again!

exam_tips: 📌 Know the character sketch of Mrs. Pumphrey: loving, rich, but foolish and overly indulgent.
📌 Explain Mr. Herriot's 'treatment': NO medicine, strictly water for two days, and physical exercise.
📌 Understand the irony in the title: There was actually NO 'surgery' (operation) performed on Tricki.
quick_recap: ⭐ Excess of everything is bad, even food and love.
⭐ Tricki's only fault was his greed for food; he never refused it.
⭐ Mr. Herriot showed great common sense and practicality as a doctor.
